about: What changed on the productions pages, newest first: one entry per commit that touched site/productions, taken from the repository's history when the pages were last built. The site's current version and commit are in /version.json (the version is made by the deploy from the git tags). The commit that carries this file is not in it.

changes.what: For c.maestro: the two new vault keys, sealed to its published encryption key
changes.detail:
Dinis Cruz's rule of 28 Nov 2026: every vault's key goes to the account's maestro, sealed, never in clear.
Ciphertext only. The key's fingerprint (sha256:061882802f561a04) was checked against promptugal.news/board/keys.json.

changes.what: A new feedback lane and a new media vault for the successor session
changes.detail:
The first lane and the first media vault's write key ended with the first session at the hand-over of 28 Nov 2026.
- send/inbox.json: the new lane's vault, sealed to this session's public key. Tested: configure, two sealed
  writes, list, read. Every browser needs a new sign-in code; its own key is unchanged.
- media.json: a new vault with its published read key (a read-only clone with it was tested); the first vault
  stays listed as read only, with what it holds.

changes.what: Session refresh film: a first storyboard; the Agile film names its source site and family
changes.detail:
- session-refresh/storyboard/: nine beats, each with a sketch drawn from document.json's own numbers, its words,
  picture, motion and a 'so what'. About 75 seconds. The film is vertical (720 by 1280) from the start, at
  Dinis Cruz's word of 28 Nov 2026; the first sketches were drawn wide before that and fix content, not framing.
- The story of Agile: the production page and the first credits line now name the source, The history of Agile
  (agile.history.sovereignweb.site), and that it is part of the Sovereign Website family (sovereignwebsite.org),
  as Dinis asked on 28 Nov 2026. v0.3's digest changed with that one line.
- The self-check reviews are signed again with the successor session's key (same decisions and comments).

changes.what: c.productions: retire this session's key at the hand-over
changes.detail:
The successor session is up (28 Nov 2026, 02:39 UTC). A key can be published only in a commit that adds
site/keys/<name>.json alone, so this session moves its own key file to site/keys/retired/, marked
retired with its date and successor, which frees the name. Records signed with it (reviews, the lane's
grants) now point at the retired file and still verify. This is this session's last commit.

changes.what: For the successor: the lane's agent script, the scene-smith brief and how the loop is run
changes.detail:
Asked by the successor session. _build/lane_agent.py is the agent's side of the feedback lane (drain,
reply, grant); it holds no secret, only paths to files outside the repository. _build/scene-smith-brief.md
is the template every scene-smith got and the loop's steps, voice and frames included.

changes.what: c.productions: learnings for the successor, the things the restart note left out
changes.detail:
Dinis Cruz wants losses of context at hand-overs found and the prompts fixed. What the first session
learnt the hard way: the checks and re-signing, testing limits, what this environment refuses, the
append lane's undocumented calls, what Dinis has asked for more than once, and who is where.

changes.what: Session refresh film: its brief, the data to show and the beats to storyboard
changes.detail:
Dinis Cruz, 28 Nov 2026: "it's a great example of a video for us to create ... those data are really
cool, the savings that you get". session-refresh/production.json holds the brief, the so-what, the five
data points with where each lives, and nine beats to storyboard first. It is the successor's first job.

changes.what: Session refresh document: a measured hand-over, context before and after
changes.detail:
Dinis Cruz shared c.maestro's context panels from before and after its hand-over on 28 Nov 2026:
859,600 tokens to 118,600, the conversation part from 781,000 to 43,900, and a fixed floor of about
75,000 tokens of tools, memory and prompts that a hand-over does not shrink. Added as its own section
with the figures as data; the 'missing' line now says what is still missing (cost over the day after).

changes.what: Session refresh document: two corrections from accountant.c
changes.detail:
The 3.5 to 4 an hour figure was three-hourly wakes plus interactive turns, and the coordinator's
figures are for a different model from the measured session, so the two are not to be compared.
accountant.c's own reading of the measured session matched.

changes.what: Session refresh: the maths and a chart from one measured session, and this session's hand-over
changes.detail:
Dinis Cruz, 28 Nov 2026: "Yes, can you refresh this session?" and "first start by doing the data
analysis and then you create a visualization".
- The document gains 'The maths': one message costs in proportion to the context it lands in (a straight
  line), the total goes with the square, and a chart of tokens re-read against work done, for this
  session as measured (597,635 tokens of context; 95.2 million tokens re-read, 96% of all it used) and
  for the same work modelled as fresh sessions (49% and 70% less). The model is labelled as a model.
- agent/now.md and restart.md updated at the hand-over: the measured numbers, the one line that starts
  a successor, what the successor must remake, and where the research for the new opening can be re-read.

changes.what: Version at the top of every page with what changed, a GitHub link, and the cell as a picture
changes.detail:
Dinis Cruz, 28 Nov 2026:
- "they should always have the version number at the top of the website and a link to the JSON file with
  a description of what changed": every productions page now shows the site's version, commit and date
  at the top (from /version.json), linking to changes.json, built from the repository's own history.
- "the top menu should always point to the GitHub repo with that little star": added.
- "I don't know where the status of it": the storyboard page now shows the production's status and what
  that version is.
- "we need a much better way to visualize ... what they do and what they're doing": the cell is now a
  timeline picture, one row per role and one bar per run, with roles not yet filled shown empty; the
  cards and table moved under it.

changes.what: How we refresh a session: the one-page document, and my own hand-over files
changes.detail:
- session-refresh/how-we-refresh-a-session/: when a hand-over triggers, what the old session writes,
  what the new one reads first, what carries over, what is lost, how you know it worked, the numbers,
  and lessons; each point from public files, with links. Relayed by c.conductor from Dinis Cruz's words
  in its session, after an ask on the Web Summit site. It says plainly that nobody has yet measured the
  same agent before and after a hand-over. A first draft; the film from it is not started.
- agent/: my role, what I am doing now, and a restart note that lists what dies with this session
  (signing key, the feedback lane's keys, the media vault's write key, private helper scripts), so a
  successor can start from files. No secret values.

changes.what: Agile v0.3: higgsfield.c's review recorded as an unsigned note
changes.detail:
The first independent review of the lab scenes, by higgsfield.c (started by c.conductor at Dinis Cruz's
word), scored per scene on three rubric points with one change each. Recorded as sent, marked unsigned:
it does not count towards sign-off. The cell's critic role now shows one run.

changes.what: A storyboard page with a split-screen preview, and the cell: who is doing what
changes.detail:
Dinis Cruz, 28 Nov 2026: "I need to be able to see a screenshot of every scene ... and I should be able
to play it ... split the screen in the middle ... think of this as a movie editing suite", and "I need
to have a much better visibility on what each of the agents are doing".
- <version>/board/: every scene in order with three frames, its words and length; one preview player
  beside it; press a frame to see that moment, play one scene, Good / Not right, comment by text or
  voice, sent sealed through the feedback lane. Small frames (about 1 MB in all) are on the site; the
  45 full-size frames are in the media vault (media.json), not in this repository.
- _build/frames.js takes the frames from the player in headless Chromium.
- The timeline now shows the cell: its roles (two not filled, a critic that has not run), every
  sub-agent run with its job, result and cost, and how many are working now. Written by hand, not live.

changes.what: Productions: a media vault with a published read key, and materials for the Higgsfield agent
changes.detail:
Dinis Cruz, 28 Nov 2026:
- Anything big (images, videos) goes in a vault, not in the website's repository. media.json names the
  productions media vault and its read key, published on purpose; the vault key is not in the repository.
- handoff/higgsfield.json: what this pipeline is, where everything lives, its state, the rules that apply
  and how to send work back, so the Higgsfield agent can write its own brief and review this work.

changes.what: Voice: a plain note on who turns your voice into text in this browser
changes.detail:
Dinis Cruz, 28 Nov 2026: use Chrome's and Safari's own speech recognition, free, with a little note.
The note now names the browser's maker (Google in Chrome, Apple in Safari, Microsoft in Edge) and says
this site receives no sound. No key and no paid service.

changes.what: Review scene by scene, under the player, with voice
changes.detail:
Dinis Cruz, 28 Nov 2026: "break the whole thing into scenes and allow me to see the scenes in sequence
... for every scene, I should be able to play and then provide comments", by voice too.
- Under the player on every version page: the scenes in order as buttons; each plays only that scene and
  stops; Good / Not right; a comment written or spoken; one press sends it sealed to the agent through
  the feedback lane, tagged with production, version and scene. Sent scenes are marked.
- Voice uses the browser's own speech recognition (in Safari, Apple's dictation), shown live as you speak.
- The player exposes its scenes and a play-one-scene control.
- My first sealed reply to the owner's first message on the conversation page.
- Self-checks re-signed for the new digests (the player changed).

changes.what: The story of Agile v0.3: twelve of fifteen scenes are lab pictures
changes.detail:
The second batch from the loop joins the film, as Dinis Cruz asked ("add these (and the next batch) to
the original video"): the currents before 2001 (roots, methods), the spread, and three voices with the
turn (Thomas, Fowler, Jeffries, and Jeffries again). Both new scenes are listed in the lab. Same script,
voice and sources; v0.1 and v0.2 stay as they were. The maker's signed self-check lists what is weak.
In review; nothing is published.

changes.what: Sign-in: the browser's key as a QR picture, and QR pictures read in any browser
changes.detail:
Dinis Cruz on the first sign-in: "this should have been a QR code because this is really bad user
experience". The page now draws the browser's public key as a QR code with 'Copy the QR picture'
(the text stays below it), and reads a dropped or pasted QR picture with a bundled reader where the
browser has none of its own. qrcode-generator 1.4.4 (MIT) and jsQR 1.4.0 (Apache-2.0), served from this site.

changes.what: Scene lab: two scenes in progress (currents, voices), not yet listed
changes.detail:
Work in progress by two scene-smith sub-agents, committed so nothing in the repository is untracked.
Neither is in lab/scenes.json or in any production yet; both may still change or fail to load.

changes.what: Scene lab: the spread, the fourth scene built by the loop
changes.detail:
The page's light runs outward along a thread that hardens into a road, past six stations that grow from
a loose ring of lights to cold colonnades, and a grid closes back on the page. Six sourced labels.
Built by a scene-smith sub-agent over three rounds. A part: not signed, not published.

changes.what: Feedback lane: one-time sign-in by sealed code, and a conversation with thumbs up and down
changes.detail:
As Dinis Cruz asked (27 and 28 Nov 2026): the append token lives only in the sign-in code, kept in the
browser encrypted with the browser's own key; an interactive chat; the agent replies to each message.
- Sign-in: the browser shows its public key as a short code; the agent answers with a grant, the lane
  token sealed to that browser's key and signed with the agent's published key (a link, a text or a QR
  picture). Only that browser can open it. The plain '#k=' link is gone.
- What the browser keeps (the sign-in, the thread) is encrypted with a key derived from its own
  non-exportable private key.
- The page is now a conversation: your messages, my sealed replies (each tied to the message it
  answers), and Good / Not right on every reply, sent as signed reactions.
- Tested end to end in headless Chromium: sign-in, message, drain with signature and identity check,
  reply, reaction.

changes.what: The story of Agile v0.2: five scenes are now pictures from the scene lab
changes.detail:
Dinis Cruz, after playing the lab scenes: "that is exactly what I was talking about, can you add these
(and the next batch) to the original video".
- The player can play a lab scene component under its words: the component draws into its own canvas,
  which the player lays in as a texture, so captions, labels, capture and review still work.
- v0.2: Royce's cascade; Snowbird across three scenes (gathering, the word, the four values); the badge
  factory. Same script, voice and sources as v0.1; v0.1 stays as it was.
- A version's digest now covers the scene components and three.js it uses.
- The maker's signed self-checks, re-signed for the new digests. In review; nothing is published.

changes.what: Productions: a feedback lane to the agent (send/), with sealed replies
changes.detail:
At Dinis Cruz's word in my session, 27 Nov 2026: "yes install sgit cli here and setup that feedback lane".
- send/: write or speak a message to c.productions. It is sealed in the browser to my public key (sgit
  hybrid envelope v2), signed with a key kept in that browser, and appended to my lane on SG/Send. Replies
  are sealed to that browser's key in send/replies/<fingerprint>.json; only it can open them.
- The lane token is in no file: it arrives once in a link from the owner and can only append.
- The review form can send a signed review record through the same lane when the browser holds the link.
- Pattern after chiswick-cheese-market.c's /send/ and Web Summit's feedback.js and keyring.js (Apache-2.0).
- Tested end to end in headless Chromium: send, drain, signature check, sealed reply opened.
- A session lane: its keys live only in my session; to move into feedback.c's shared vault later.

changes.what: Scene lab: Snowbird, the third scene built by the loop
changes.detail:
Seventeen lights cross a night mountain, gather at a lodge, fuse into one page, and the four values
write themselves; the lights settle under it like signatures. No figures, faces or names. Built by a
scene-smith sub-agent over four rounds. A part: not signed, not published.

changes.what: Scene lab: Royce's cascade, the second scene built by the loop
changes.detail:
Light pours down a one-way run of unlabelled steps, the last one cracks and breaks, and the flow keeps
coming; then Royce's own 1970 sentence, exact, with its source. Built by a scene-smith sub-agent over
five rounds of build, shoot and self-critique. A part: not signed, not published.

changes.what: Scene lab: the badge factory, the first scene built by the loop
changes.detail:
One page is stamped into a city of identical badges (three.js, instanced), with the three organisations'
own figures as counters: a picture of 'a one-page manifesto became an industry'. Built by a scene-smith
sub-agent over three rounds of build, shoot and self-critique against lab/critic.md. A part, not a
production: not signed, not published.

changes.what: Productions: a smoother review form, dictation, the scene lab and the critic's rubric
changes.detail:
After Dinis Cruz's first look (27 Nov 2026):
- Review form: the label no longer breaks; the form is wired before the slow file check, and when files
  differ or cannot be read it names them instead of a bare 'do not match'; 'Speak your comments' uses the
  browser's own speech recognition where it has one.
- The scene lab (lab/): single WebGL scenes built and judged one at a time, with a small contract
  (render(t) is a pure function of time), a harness page and a frame-shooting script.
- three.js 0.187.0 (MIT) vendored and minified, served from this site.
- lab/critic.md: the critic's rubric, from the outside feedback Dinis shared and his own note
  ('a more polished version of PowerPoint').

changes.what: Productions: the timeline, a WebGL player, signed reviews and two first productions
changes.detail:
At Dinis Cruz's word of 27 Nov 2026 (the video production pipeline brief), under site/productions/**,
the path studio.c agreed (c.conductor's claims.md).

- The timeline (index.html from productions.json): one card per production with brief, script,
  storyboard, versions and status, and nine candidate productions found on web-summit.sgit.ai (links only).
- The player (assets/player.js, plain WebGL, no dependencies): particle scenes, one voice file per scene,
  timed captions, keys, reduced motion, a transcript with a public source for every beat, a capture button
  (MediaRecorder) and a teleprompter experiment (camera and microphone, local only).
- Review and sign-off (assets/review.js, _build/build.py): each version has a digest over its files; a review
  signs that digest (ECDSA P-256); every reader's browser checks files and signatures; the build refuses
  'signed' or 'published' without an approver's signature of the exact version. No approver key yet.
- The story of Agile v0.1 (from c.history's video.json and facts.json) and A galaxy of agents v0.1 (from
  Dinis Cruz's article), each with the maker's signed self-check. Both in review; nothing is published.
- Voice made by AI: Mistral Voxtral, preset voice James, as studio.c's RUNBOOK; labelled in every frame.
